messages:
maya: Alert from infra-audit: spike of KMS Decrypts for cmk-analytics (us-west-2) from analytics-service-account around 13:03 UTC. Not expected. :rotating_light:

tom: linking PR that touched auth mappings earlier today — https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/+/842 — @akash was the author, right?

akash: yep that was my RBAC refactor to consolidate dataset roles. I ran the migration script but didn’t expect it to touch legacy bindings.

maya: quick check shows a RoleBinding named `analytics-legacy-access` was updated to include `storage.viewer` which grants KMS decrypt via the policy we migrated.

akash: ugh. the migration does a rename + reconcile, it may have matched on label and added the new role. I’m on it.

tilly: mitigation plan: remove that RoleBinding immediately from prod, create a scoped role limiting to list/get (no kms:Decrypt), and rotate any short-lived creds that might have leaked.

maya: suggested command to revoke binding now:
```bash
kubectl --context=prod -n analytics delete rolebinding analytics-legacy-access || true
```

akash: cannot delete without SRE approval? our policy requires two approvals for prod RBAC changes. can we do an emergency override? @tilly can you approve?

tilly: approving emergency override for this binding only. maya, go for delete and paste output here. :thumbsup:

maya: ran it, output:
```
rolebinding.rbac.authorization.k8s.io "analytics-legacy-access" deleted
```

sec-bot: Security automation: emergency_RBAC_revoke executed by maya; ticket SEC-2026-138 created and attached.

tom: good. now need to scope down the role and rebind properly. akash can you push the scoped Role YAML? keep kms permissions out.

akash: pushing scoped role now, will apply as a canary in staging then prod once SRE confirms. snippet I’m applying:
```yaml
kind: Role
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: analytics-minimal-read
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["pods","configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get","list"]
```

maya: also ran cloudtrail search for s3:GetObject and found ~37 GetObject events from that service account between 13:03-13:09 UTC. Files appear to be metadata CSVs, not full dumps, but still need confirmation.

tilly: ok capture snapshot of object names and run a quick content hash to check for exfil. use the internal forensic bucket and tag.

akash: KMS console shows decrypt calls for cmk-analytics at 13:04 and 13:06 by analytics-service-account. I recommend immediate CMK rotate/disable decrypt for that principal and submit key policy deny for that identity. Will draft KMS deny now.

maya: quick command I used to scan CloudTrail events:
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=Username,AttributeValue=analytics-service-account --start-time 2026-03-18T13:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-18T13:10:00Z
```

sec-bot: Reminder: follow incident runbook steps 1-7. Postmortem owner required.

tilly: action items
- akash: create and apply CMK deny for analytics-service-account + open key rotation request (ASAP)
- maya: archive the 37 objects to forensics bucket + compute hashes + attach to SEC-2026-138
- tom: notify infra-sre for approval to rebind minimal role once validated
- sec: start customer-notification checklist if any sensitive objects confirmed

akash: acknowledged, starting CMK deny and rotation ticket. will comment with ARN and policy diff once applied.

maya: done forensics snapshot uploaded to s3://forensics-usw2/SEC-2026-138/ and hashes posted to the ticket. initial check shows no PII columns in those CSVs but we’re continuing deeper scan.

tom: thanks. keep this thread updated. once CMK deny is live we should monitor for any retry attempts and look for lateral access signs.

tilly: I’ll own the postmortem and timeline. we’ll aim for a short internal write-up by EOD and a full postmortem in 48h. good work triaging fast. :lock:
